content_sections.body: Use this lesson language to communicate a simple real-life meaning: Name common places and say where you go. Model: “The library is near the park, and the bank is opposite it.” Notice the important words and the word order. Mẹo tiếng Việt: hãy hiểu ý của cả câu trước, rồi nói theo cụm ngắn; không cần dịch từng từ.
content_sections.title: Form and meaning

content_sections.body: Read this short situation. A learner needs to use places in town clearly and politely. One useful response is: “The library is near the park, and the bank is opposite it.” Say the model once, then change one safe detail such as a name, place, time, colour, or item when the meaning allows.
content_sections.title: Guided context

content_sections.body: Practise for meaning, not only for memory. Imagine one everyday situation where places in town is useful. First use the model, then make one small change. Check: Is the message clear? Is the target language in the right place? Can another person answer you?

speaking.goal: Complete a short, understandable exchange about places in town.
speaking.instruction: Roleplay: you are a learner using places in town; the tutor is a helpful conversation partner. Scenario: you need to use this language in a short everyday interaction. Tutor opening: “Hello. Can we practise places in town?” Reply naturally, ask or answer one follow-up question, and finish the exchange politely. Useful model: The library is near the park, and the bank is opposite it.

writing.goal: Produce a short A1 message about places in town with a clear meaning.
writing.instruction: Write 2–3 short sentences for a real-life situation about places in town. Include one sentence pattern from this lesson, then add one true or invented detail. Do not copy this model exactly: The library is near the park, and the bank is opposite it. Submit your draft first.
